page.text:
Now we've started to describe a set, but we need to communicate that a
set has *set membership* capability. We do that with the `Requires:`
section.

```mlg
[\set]
Defines: X
Requires:
. capability: x_ "in" X :-> \\abstract
Enables:
. from: Y ::= {y__ : ...}
  capability: x_ "in" X :-> x_ member_of Y
Documented:
. called: "set"
Id: "a0759217-e1f6-412c-982a-0038cd17a3a1"
```

The `Requires:` is where you communicate that a concept has additional
capabilities that introduce new symbols or are operations (like `*` for
example).

In Mathlingua one writes `X is \set` to introduce the new symbol `X` and
specify it is of type is a `\set`. The form `<name> "op" <symbol>` is
called a specification and can be thought of as a function that reduces
down to an `<name> is <type>` form.

For example, if `X` is a set of `\real` numbers than `"in"` could be
defined such that `x "in" X` reduces to `x is \real`.

Here we say that a set has the concept of `"in"` which represents set
membership and the definition of the membership is on the right hand side
of `:->`. The built-in `\\abstract` represents that the specification is
abstract an sub-types of `\set` need to fill in the details.

Now we can state the definition of a set:
